    //==
    // # The public trigonometric surface on `Angle`
    //
    // `Angle` (`quantities.types.plato`) stores radians, and the scalar
    // trigonometric kernel is declared over radians-as-`Number` in
    // `intrinsics.library.plato`. This library is the thin, portable layer between
    // them: every function here unwraps `Radians`, calls the scalar intrinsic, and
    // re-wraps where the result is angular.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * Angular results are `Angle`, never raw `Number`
    //     (CONVENTIONS.md - angles). The inverse family (`Acos`, `Asin`, `Atan`,
    //     `Atan2`, ...) therefore returns `Angle`, delegating to the `*Radians`
    //     intrinsics that differ only in return type.
    //   * `SinCos` returns the pair in (Sin, Cos) order, matching `MathF.SinCos`
    //     and the host `AngleIntrinsics.SinCos`.
    //   * The arithmetic and ordering members restate, at `Angle`, what the generic
    //     `IQuantity` bodies give every quantity type; they exist because these exact
    //     signatures were host intrinsics.
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigonometric_functions

    //==
    // # Construction

    // The angle of the given number of radians. The one cast into `Angle`;
    // other units go through the conversions below (`Turns`, `Degrees`, ...).
    Angle(x: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(x);
